title: Decision for a low degree junta node
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $P\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let the failure parameter lie in $(0,1/2]$, and take a batch of the prescribed restricted sample size of free-coordinate sign assignments and labels. If the batch yields a detected frequency, choose a free coordinate in its support. Otherwise form the low-degree polynomial hypothesis from the batch: if it has a nonzero nonconstant monomial, choose a free coordinate in that monomial's support; if it has none, return the constant sign given by its coefficient at the empty set.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite set of coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
batch is indexed by the prescribed restricted sample count and contains free-coordinate assignments and sign labels
caveat: The formal statement relies on frequency-detection and coordinate-conversion constructions whose definitions are not supplied, so their precise meaning cannot be stated here.
